summary: Small World is a light area-control game where you pilot a string of fantasy races, expand across a too-small map by conquest, and then voluntarily send your civilization into decline to launch a fresh one while still scoring from the old. Turns are quick and aggressive, with constant skirmishing over the same cramped territories.
praised: the decline mechanic that keeps every race useful even in defeat
huge replayability from randomized race/power combinations
fast, easy to teach, works well with non-gamers
genuinely funny and thematic race/power names
criticised: combat resolution leans on a die that can undercut careful planning
map can favor whoever is dealt strong combos
runs a bit long for how light the decisions are with 5 players

interaction.detail: Players attack directly onto the same shared map to take each other's territories, so board space is a constant fight rather than parallel development. Whose race is in decline and who is expanding shifts the balance of power every round.

win_criteria: Most points, one or two sources

scoring.why: Every round's score is just the number of regions your active and declining races occupy, tallied turn after turn, with leftover victory coins as a minor tie-breaker resource.
scoring.how_you_win: Each turn you score points equal to the territories your race(s) control, choosing when to let a race 'go into decline' to start a fresh one; the highest cumulative total after the last turn wins.
